title: Verb groups and the て-form
summary: Verbs come in three groups. Each group has its own recipe for the て-form and the た-form.

blocks.text: To make the て-form (and the past た-form, which follows the very same rules) you first need to know which of three groups a verb belongs to.
Ichidan verbs end in **いる** or **える**, and conjugation is easy: **drop る and add the ending**. 食べる becomes 食べて and 食べた. 見る becomes 見て and 見た.

This is the biggest group. A godan verb can end in **any** う-row sound, and the て-form depends on that last kana. Careful: some verbs that end in いる or える are godan, not ichidan: 帰る (to return) and 走る (to run) are godan.

blocks.title: How godan verbs make the て-form

blocks.text: The た-form works the same way with た (and だ after ん and いで): 飲む→飲んだ, 歩く→歩いた, 泳ぐ→泳いだ. 死ぬ is the only verb that ends in ぬ. One exception: **行く** becomes **行って**, not 行いて.
Only two: **来る** (to come, て-form 来て) and **する** (to do, て-form して).

items: **Godan**: look at the last kana (**う つ る → って**, **ぬ ぶ む → んで**, **く → いて**, **ぐ → いで**, **す → して**).
**行く → 行って** is the one godan exception.
Irregular: **来る → 来て**, **する → して**.
Do not trust the look of a verb: **帰る** and **走る** are godan.
